educanada-study-in-canada-scholarships-2.about:
This Global Affairs Canada programme supports short-term exchanges for study or research in Canada by students who remain enrolled and paying tuition at their home institution. Values: CAD 10,200 for one term; CAD 14,000 for 5-6 months (graduate). Eligible: Bangladesh, Nepal, Taiwan, Türkiye, Ukraine, Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda (2026-27 list).

Students cannot apply directly: a Canadian post-secondary institution selects the student and submits the nomination through the My EduCanada portal (usually with a tuition waiver or exchange arrangement). The 2026-27 cycle closed with an institutional deadline of 31 March 2026; the programme runs every year, so students should approach a Canadian partner university or professor in late 2026 / early 2027 for the 2027-28 cycle.
highlights: Funding: CAD 10,200 for one term; CAD 14,000 for 5-6 months (graduate)
For full-time students at home institutions
Nominated by a Canadian college or university
educanada-study-in-canada-scholarships-2.eligibility: Citizens of eligible countries (Bangladesh, Nepal, Taiwan, Türkiye, Ukraine, Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda (2026-27 list)) enrolled full-time and paying tuition at a post-secondary institution in that country; not Canadian citizens/PR; not already in a Canadian degree programme or holding other Canadian government funding.

Ask its international office to nominate you in the next EduCanada cycle
Prepare passport/ID, enrolment letter, signed privacy notice (and letters required for your programme)
The Canadian institution submits via My EduCanada
educanada-study-in-canada-scholarships-2.costs: Scholarship CAD 10,200 for one term; CAD 14,000 for 5-6 months (graduate) towards travel, living and visa costs; home tuition continues.

ellehacks-2027.about:
ElleHacks 2027 is Canada's largest hackathon for women and gender-diverse students. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at York University in Toronto from 2027-01-29 to 2027-01-31. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Free entry, food and mentoring
Official MLH 2027 season event
Build a portfolio project in one weekend

Attend in person and submit your project for judging
ellehacks-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

epfl-life-sciences-summer-research-progr.about:
The Summer Research Program of EPFL's School of Life Sciences places international bachelor's and first-year master's students in an EPFL research group in Lausanne (or Geneva) for eight weeks of hands-on lab work, from 5 July to 27 August 2027. Fields include biology, biophysics, chemistry, bioengineering, bioinformatics and quantitative biology.

Each student receives CHF 3,600 for the two months (housing in shared student accommodation near campus is deducted in advance, leaving about CHF 1,700 to live on), and travel to Switzerland is reimbursed up to CHF 1,000 for overseas flights or CHF 500 for shorter trips. Only 20–25 students are selected, so a clear research motivation and a strong referee letter matter.
highlights: Real research project in an EPFL life-sciences lab
CHF 3,600 stipend plus travel reimbursement
Only 20–25 places: small, well-supported cohort
epfl-life-sciences-summer-research-progr.eligibility: International bachelor's or first-year master's students in life sciences or related fields (biology, biophysics, chemistry, bioengineering, bioinformatics, quantitative biology). Open to students worldwide.
how_to_apply: Read the programme description and FAQs (they explain the updated application form and essay topics)
Prepare your transcript and short-answer essays
Ask a referee to write a letter
Apply on the EPFL recruiting portal by 15 November 2026, 23:59 CET
epfl-life-sciences-summer-research-progr.costs: Stipend CHF 3,600 for two months (housing paid from this); travel reimbursed up to CHF 1,000 (overseas) or CHF 500 (shorter distances). No tuition.

esa-academy-ladybird-guide-spacecraft-co.about:
The 11th edition of this ESA Academy course takes place at ESA ESEC in Transinne/Redu, Belgium. An engineer from ESA's Mission Operations Department (ESOC) teaches how spacecraft communication systems are designed and operated, with real stories of rescuing missions; students use the OPS-SAT Space Lab to simulate operations with their own spacecraft and then troubleshoot a real-life anomaly.

Only 30 students are selected. ESA sponsors accommodation, meals and up to EUR 350 of travel to Belgium.

Hands-on simulated operations with OPS-SAT Space Lab
Accommodation, meals and up to EUR 350 travel paid by ESA

esa-cansat-2026-27.about:
In CanSat, a team of students designs and builds a mini-satellite that fits inside a can, with a primary mission (measuring air temperature and pressure during descent) and a secondary mission of their own choosing. Teams follow ESA's resources on Arduino, radio and parachutes, and launch their CanSat at a national competition.

Over 25 countries in Europe and Canada host national competitions (Latvia and Switzerland are new this year); each sets its own registration deadline, typically in the autumn. National winners join the CanSat Space Engineering Summit at ESA's technical centre.
highlights: Build and launch a mini-satellite
National competitions in 25+ countries
Winners go to ESA's ESTEC

Launch it at the national competition

esa-moon-camp-2026-27.about:

Teams choose their complexity level and design tool (from crafts to 3D printing and immersive worlds) and submit a project with explanations.

Every submitting team receives a participation certificate and an invitation to a final online livestream with an astronaut. National ESERO offices provide local support.

esc-accueil-famenne-rochefort-2028.about:
Accueil Famenne is a non profit organisation whose social aim is to welcome, accompany and support people whose basic needs are barely or not met, without any distinction of origins or believes. It aims to promote fraternity, solidarity, equality and social justice in Rochefort and surroundings. Accueil Famenne has three main axis: – A hosting venue “L’élan“ for single-parent families and isolated and financially disadvantaged people – A food bank for people of Rochefort and surrounding facing financial difficulties – A second hand shop “Li Gurnî“ working according to circular economy principles; providing affordable house items, whose benefits goes to financially support to two first axis. Accueil Famenne works with economically disadvantaged and/or morally isolated people. It adresses its first activity to any adult and family in Brussels and Wallonia, while the food bank is destined to people from Rochefort and surroundings.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps individual volunteering hosted by Accueil Famenne in Rochefort, Belgium; activity period 1 February 2027 – 31 January 2028. Themes: anti-discrimination and environment and nature. Application deadline: 8 November 2026. Open to young people aged 18–30 resident in 29 eligible countries (see eligibility).

Living and learning: The volunteers will have a private room in a fully-equipped shared house in the city of Rochefort with other ESC volunteers (Depending on which house you live, you’ll be 250 or 650m away). Food: the volunteer will receive a budget and will take care of the meals by themself. Participation in the ESC is free of charge for the participant, except for exceptional contribution to travel costs. The volunteer will receive free board and lodging during the whole activity. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Free for the volunteer: travel, housing, food, pocket money and insurance covered by the European Solidarity Corps

esc-across-laane-harjus-youth-padise-202.about:
Lääne-Harju Youth and Cultural Center is a public youth center located in the north-western part of Estonia, working with young people through various educational and cultural activities. The organisation coordinates the work of seven youth rooms based in different small towns. Local young people aged 7-26 are welcome to join wide range of leisure activities organised by the permanent staff. The volunteers will be assisting a team of youth workers in daily activities of the centers in various locations giving a chance to see many places including beautiful nature and meet people around Lääne-Harju county. The youth worker provide task related support and guidance to the volunteers. Developing ideas and taking initiative is encouraged and fostered. Lääne-Harju Youth and Cultural Center is open to host international volunteers who would become part of their community. FOR MORE INFORMATION & HOW TO APPLY:

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Lääne-Harju Kultuuri- ja Noortekeskus in Padise, Estonia; activity period up to 11 months (1 September 2026 – 31 July 2027). Topics: social inclusion and community work, civic participation, health and wellbeing, education and non-formal learning, employment and entrepreneurship, culture and creativity, sport and physical activity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 37 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: The volunteers will be housed in a shared flat in a small town in Keila which is located near Tallinn. All the necessities are provided in the apartment. There is a frequent bus and train connection between villages in the area as well with the capital. Volunteers receive €5/day pocket money and additional €7/day food allowance, managing their own meals. International travel is reimbursed based on set travel budget and task related local transport is covered to full extent. Team at Lääne-Harju Youth Centers is made up of professional youth workers who are dedicated to supporting the personal development of volunteers throughout their stay. They are ready to offer support, coaching and assistance with adjusting and shaping the experience. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

esc-climate-change-adaptation-tamale-202.about:
Mondo Estonia is sending a volunteer to Northern Ghana, where communities face persistent poverty and heavy dependence on rain-fed agriculture. Climate change is worsening these challenges through erratic rainfall, drought, rising temperatures, and flooding, with serious effects on farming, water security, livelihoods, and employment. Rural communities therefore need both immediate adaptation measures and long-term resilience-building strategies. The volunteer will support key activities including conducting climate vulnerability assessments, identifying practical intervention options, building local capacity in energy saving, reduce-reuse-repair-recycle practices, food management, income diversification, and sustainable farming using organic inputs, as well as strengthening networking and stakeholder engagement in climate action.

esc-connect-create-kc-klastor-roznava-20.about:
KC Kláštor is a vibrant cultural and community center in the heart of Rožňava, a town in eastern Slovakia known for its historical architecture, proximity to the Slovak Karst, and a peaceful yet open community atmosphere. As a volunteer, you will support the center's team in organizing cultural events, workshops, and community activities for people of all ages. You will be part of a team that runs the accommodation, café, kitchen, and of course, cultural programming, aiming to contribute to the development of the local community. We warmly welcome your own ideas, skills, and cultural perspectives. The center prides itself on an open and inclusive environment where every idea and every person has a place. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience in community development and cultural management, build confidence in working with people, and experience everyday life in a small yet lively Slovak town close to nature.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Otvor Dvor in Rožňava, Slovakia; activity period up to 12 months (1 September 2026 – 1 September 2027). Topics: civic participation, health and wellbeing, employment and entrepreneurship, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 43 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: We will provide volunteers with suitable accommodation located directly on the host organization's premises, featuring a private room with a shared kitchen and bathroom. Volunteers receive pocket money of €5 per day and a food allowance of €7 per day, and are responsible for preparing their own meals. International travel costs are reimbursed within the set budget, and local transport related to your duties is fully covered. Volunteers will take part in the ESC training cycle organized by the Slovak National Agency, which focuses on personal development and intercultural learning. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

As a volunteer you can support SEEDS in their international camps in one of the three roles that fits you best! 1)Environment Camp Leaders assist the Project Manager in planning, implementing and participating in SEEDS’ nature camps and learning camps in Iceland. 2) Photography Camp Leaders assist the Project Manager in planning, implementing and participating in SEEDS’ Photography, Social & Environmental Issues in Iceland Camps. 3) Based in the SEEDS office in Reykjavík, the Communications & PR Volunteer assists the Project Manager in facilitating communication links between staff and other volunteers (short and long-term) as well as local and partner organisations from other countries.

esc-creative-workshops-seniors-social-gd.about:
Social Welfare Home in Gdynia is a residential care home for elderly people who need daily support. Some residents may have difficulties with moving around, taking care of their health, or managing everyday tasks, so they are supported by professional staff. The home is located in a cosy and green area, close to a forest, and has its own garden. It is home to 79 residents who form a small community. For them, it is important not only to receive care, but also to have social contact, stay active, and feel included. The centre offers different activities that help residents maintain their physical and mental wellbeing. These include rehabilitation, therapeutic activities, Senior Club meetings, and various social and cultural events. As a volunteer, you will mainly support occupational therapy activities. This type of therapy helps residents stay active, develop their interests, and enjoy their time. You will also help organise holidays and special events.

Volunteers will support activities at Tránsito Amaguaña School, in Mercade Mayorista in Quito. Tasks include: -Educational and classroom support, daily tutoring and learning reinforcement to children at the school, supporting teachers during lessons, assisting children with reading, writing, and basic math, preparing simple educational materials, and helping with small group or one-on-one activities. -SkillBoost workshops: Every three months, you help facilitate a workshop on topics like peace, digital literacy, innovation or higher education. -Youth circles: You will assist in organizing and facilitating peer group sessions focused on emotional well-being, identity and shared challenges. esc-cross-culture-cooperation-solidarity.about:
We welcome volunteer artists from EU countries, aged 18-30, in fields such as music, dance, painting, photography, pottery, weaving and traditional crafts. Our organization promotes these crafts in Roma communities and works with young people and adolescents. The volunteer program offers an opportunity to interact with a different culture - one where music and dance are the most captivating forms of entertainment, interaction and joy. Our goal is to build an intercultural bridge between Roma and non-Roma youth. We hope that this project will serve as a model of fruitful cooperation, inclusion and community responsibility. We invite you to join us for a unique volunteering experience! With our support, you will: - Organize and conduct workshops for Roma teenagers on various topics: freedom of expression through art/crafts/personal development/ESC/Erasmus+ opportunities/health/environment/civic education/human rights. - Learn and apply non-formal education methods.
